papers.title: Sequential Learning under Informational Ambiguity

authors.inst: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.q: Do information cascades arise robustly in sequential social learning when individuals are ambiguity averse?
papers.summary: With sufficient ambiguity, cascades arise almost surely regardless of signal structure statistics. Even minimal ambiguity can trigger cascades with bounded signals and lead to incorrect herding with unbounded signals.
papers.contribution: Studies sequential learning with ambiguity about others' signal structures and max-min expected utility, showing cascades are robust.
papers.ident: Theory: sequential social learning under max-min expected utility with ambiguity about signal structures.

papers.title: Risk Preferences and Field Behavior: The Relevance of Higher-Order Risk Preferences
papers.q: Do higher-order risk preferences such as prudence and temperance explain field behavior beyond risk aversion?
papers.contribution: Measures intensities of prudence and temperance using new methods in an incentivized experiment with 658 adolescents.
papers.summary: Higher-order risk preferences are strongly related to prevention, health, addictive behavior and financial decisions. Ignoring them can give misleading conclusions about risk preferences, and survey risk tolerance often captures them.
papers.ident: Incentivized experiment measuring prudence and temperance, related to field behavior.
papers.dataDetail: Incentivized experiment and field behavior data for 658 adolescents.

papers.title: Do resource rents drive urbanization and structural transformation? A global analysis
papers.q: Do resource rents drive urbanization and structural transformation globally?
papers.summary: Studies whether resource rents drive urbanization and structural transformation, in a global analysis.

papers.title: Monetary Cooperation during Global Inflation Surges
papers.q: How should monetary policy be set, and coordinated, during global scarcity of tradable goods?
papers.summary: The optimal response is an inflation surge that rebalances production toward tradables. The inflation costs are borne domestically while higher tradable supply partly spills over abroad, so national central banks may over-tighten and cause an unnecessarily sharp global contraction.
papers.contribution: Studies optimal monetary policy in a global scarcity of tradables and shows how the spillover of its gains creates a coordination trap.
papers.ident: Theory: open-economy model of optimal monetary policy under global tradable goods scarcity.

papers.title: Commercial rivalry as seller incidence shifting: Non-parametric accounting of the China shock
papers.summary: Studies commercial rivalry as a shift in seller incidence, with a non-parametric accounting of the China shock.

papers.title: Uncovering mild drift in asset prices with intraday high-frequency data
papers.q: Can mild drift in asset prices be detected with intraday high-frequency data?
papers.contribution: Studies realized squared drift and the drift-robust quarticity estimator RiceQ under twin asymptotics, and proposes consistent drift tests across constant, linear, trending and bursting drift.
papers.summary: Conditions are identified for realized squared drift to gauge integrated squared drift when the time span is large enough, and RiceQ stays consistent under twin asymptotics subject to divergence rate constraints.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: drift estimation and testing in drift-diffusion models with high-frequency data.

papers.title: Tying with Network Effects
papers.q: How can tying leverage consumer surplus in markets with network effects?
papers.summary: Tying emerges as a best response without precommitment and lowers the quality of tied-market rivals. It can exclude rivals but can also expand use of the tying product, so welfare effects are ambiguous.
papers.ident: Theory: model of tying with network effects.
papers.contribution: Develops a leverage theory of tying where unexploited consumer surplus creates a quasi-installed base advantage in a network-effect market.

papers.title: Strategic network formation with many agents
papers.q: How can the distribution of links in strategic network formation be approximated with many agents?
papers.summary: The link frequency distribution from finite pairwise stable networks converges to a limiting distribution characterized by aggregate equilibrium conditions that may permit multiple solutions. Identification of link preferences is analyzed and an estimation method proposed.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: random utility model of strategic network formation with many-player asymptotics.
papers.contribution: Derives a tractable approximation to link distributions in a random utility model with many-player asymptotics, with no restriction on selection among multiple stable networks.

papers.title: Anatomy of the Greek Depression with Firm-Level Data: The Importance of Demand Shocks

authors.inst: Athens University of Economics and Business
Athens University of Economics and Business

papers.summary: During a 22% output decline, young and small firms had steeper sales growth declines, largely from adverse demand shocks intensified by financing constraints. Their disproportionate impact accounts for about one-quarter of the total output decline.
papers.q: What explained the steeper sales declines of young and small firms in the Greek Depression?
papers.contribution: Uses firm-level data to separate demand shocks from financing constraints and their interaction.
papers.ident: Firm-level analysis of sales growth with demand shocks and financing constraints.
papers.dataDetail: Greek firm-level data during the Greek Depression.

papers.title: Mental Accounts and Consumption Sensitivity across the Distribution of Liquid Assets
papers.q: How do consumption responses to predictable income vary across liquid asset holdings, and can mental accounts explain them?
papers.summary: Even households with large liquid balances show no spending before income receipt, substantial spending after and front-loading by date of receipt. The model reproduces the timing, magnitude and cross-section of responses and is used to evaluate fiscal stimulus policies.
papers.ident: Event-time analysis of spending around predictable income receipt, with a structural mental accounts model.
papers.contribution: Uses household-level data from a US financial institution and develops a mental accounts model partitioning choices across current income and assets.
papers.dataDetail: Household-level data from a US financial institution.

papers.title: Uncertainty and the Economy: The Evolving Distributions of Aggregate Supply and Demand Shocks
papers.q: How have the distributions of aggregate supply and demand shocks evolved, including bad uncertainty?
papers.summary: The Great Moderation is driven by lower volatility of supply shocks and the Gaussian component of demand shocks. Greater bad demand uncertainty has lowered the conditional skewness of GDP growth and inflation, and the correlation between inflation and growth shocks has risen due to lower supply volatility.
papers.contribution: Estimates time-varying distributions of aggregate supply and demand shocks and separates Gaussian from negatively skewed bad uncertainty.
papers.ident: Time series: estimated time-varying distributions of supply and demand shocks with skewness.
papers.dataDetail: Macroeconomic series on GDP growth and inflation.

papers.title: ‘Less Is More’: Consumer Spending and the Size of Economic Stimulus Payments
papers.q: How does consumption respond to transitory income gains of different sizes?
papers.summary: Affluent households have higher MPCs out of large gains, while liquidity-poor families have higher MPCs out of small gains. Non-homothetic preferences fit higher earners and borrowing constraints fit low-income households.
papers.contribution: Uses hypothetical questions from the Italian Survey of Household Income and Wealth to compare marginal propensities to consume across gain sizes and households.
papers.conclusion: For a given fiscal outlay, smaller transfers to a broader group of low-income households stimulate aggregate consumption more than larger transfers to fewer recipients.
papers.ident: Survey experiment: hypothetical income gain questions of different sizes.
papers.dataDetail: Italian Survey of Household Income and Wealth.

papers.title: The Economics of Climate Innovation: Technology, Climate Policy, and the Clean Energy Transition

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.summary: Outlines incentives, market failures and policy levers for clean technology development and diffusion, and traces global patterns in development and deployment.
papers.q: What incentives, market failures and policies shape the development and diffusion of clean technologies?
papers.contribution: Reviews the economics of climate innovation and its frontier challenges in adaptation, critical minerals, artificial intelligence and geopolitics.
papers.conclusion: Effective climate policy needs coordinated approaches that match instruments to technology maturity and local context.

papers.title: Human Capital and Development
papers.q: What is the role of human capital in growth, innovation and poverty reduction at different stages of development?
papers.summary: Different types of human capital matter at different stages of development. Despite more years of schooling, the poorest regions still see stagnating learning and quality, potentially creating poverty traps.
papers.contribution: Reviews macro and micro evidence on human capital and development, with a simple framework for obstacles to accumulation and evidence from randomized interventions.
papers.conclusion: Policies that remove barriers to skill acquisition can establish foundations for sustained growth.

papers.title: Cross-product and cross-market adjustments within multiproduct firms: Evidence from antidumping actions

authors.inst: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

papers.q: How do targeted antidumping actions affect a multiproduct firm's prices and quantities across its other products and destinations?
papers.contribution: Uses Chinese firm-product export data to document within-firm cross-product trade deflection and a within-firm chilling effect.
papers.summary: An antidumping duty on one product in one destination is associated with lower prices and higher sales of the firm's other products across all markets, which depends on rising joint production costs. An antidumping action in one destination also leads the firm to raise price and lower quantity of the same product elsewhere.
papers.ident: Firm-product-destination analysis of the effects of antidumping actions on a firm's other products and markets.
papers.dataDetail: Chinese firm-product-level export data.

papers.title: The Economics of Equilibrium with Indivisible Goods
papers.q: When does competitive equilibrium exist with indivisible goods?
papers.summary: Gives sufficient and essentially necessary conditions for equilibrium existence entirely in terms of demand.
papers.contribution: Develops a theory of equilibrium with indivisible goods based on complementarity and substitutability between bundles, unifying complements and substitutes settings.
papers.conclusion: The analysis has implications for auction design.
papers.ident: Theory: competitive equilibrium existence with indivisible goods.

papers.title: New Keynesian Economics with Household and Firm Heterogeneity
papers.q: How can firm heterogeneity be incorporated into heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models?
papers.contribution: Provides a framework and benchmark heterogeneous-firm model where financial frictions generate high marginal propensities to invest, analogous to high MPCs.
papers.summary: High MPIs activate transmission channels through after-tax-and-transfer cash flows, as high MPCs do for households. There is no consensus on credible estimates of the MPI distribution, so the paper surveys the modelling choices that shape it.
papers.ident: Quantitative: heterogeneous-firm HANK framework with financial frictions.

papers.title: The Long Run Economic Effects of Medical Innovation and the Role of Opportunities
papers.q: What are the long-run effects of early childhood pneumonia on adult outcomes, and how do opportunities shape them?
papers.summary: There are large average gains in education, employment, income and disability outcomes. Black men have smaller schooling gains but larger employment and earnings gains than white men, and Black individuals born in more discriminatory Jim Crow states gain much less. Women gain less than men in education and earnings.
papers.ident: Introduction of the first antibiotic therapies in 1937 as variation in early childhood pneumonia exposure by birth cohort.
papers.contribution: Exploits the 1937 introduction of antibiotic therapies and census data to study heterogeneity by race, gender and Jim Crow discrimination.
papers.conclusion: Opportunities shape how early-life health investments translate into longer-run economic gains.
papers.dataDetail: US census data on cohorts born around 1937, with race, gender and state of birth.

papers.title: Spousal Social Security Claiming Decisions and the Financial Shock of Widowhood
papers.summary: Widowhood is a major financial shock for older women. Women whose husbands delayed claiming to full retirement age face a 15.6 percentage point increase in the probability of falling below the 5th percentile of pre-widowhood living standards, and this effect is about 6.3% smaller for each year of delay, concentrated 5-8 years after.
papers.ident: Staggered difference-in-differences around widowhood, comparing by husband's Social Security claiming age.
papers.q: How does spousal Social Security claiming affect the financial shock of widowhood?
papers.contribution: Updates the widowhood financial shock with staggered difference-in-differences methods and relates it to husbands' delayed claiming.

papers.title: Open Devices and Slices: Evidence From Wi-Fi Equipment
papers.contribution: Exploits the staggered introduction of open drivers in router supply chains with novel data on all routers and subcomponents from 2000 to 2018.
papers.summary: Openness enhances supplier autonomy, increases new product introductions and puts more products near the technical frontier. The largest component suppliers benefit from greater sales, and there is no evidence it helps entrants, small firms or assemblers.
papers.ident: Staggered introduction of open drivers in router supply chains as quasi-natural experiments.
papers.q: Does openness of components in supply chains raise product introductions in Wi-Fi equipment?
papers.dataDetail: Novel data on all routers and subcomponents introduced 2000-2018.

papers.title: Disadvantaging Rivals: Vertical Integration in the Pharmaceutical Market
papers.q: Did vertical integration between insurers and PBMs harm rival insurers in Medicare Part D?
papers.summary: Vertical integration in Medicare Part D increased over time. Rival insurers' premiums rose after the merger, consistent with input foreclosure, and there is no evidence of lower premiums for the merged firm's consumers.
papers.contribution: Uses a unique dataset on insurer-PBM contracts and evaluates a large 2015 insurer-PBM merger.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences around a 2015 insurer-PBM merger comparing rival insurers' premiums.
papers.dataDetail: Insurer-PBM contract data and Medicare Part D premiums.

papers.title: Exogenous consideration and extended random utility
papers.summary: With bounded observable utility shifters all three models are observationally equivalent, with the same counterfactual bounds and welfare formulas under price-like variation. Welfare cannot change in the full consideration model but is unbounded in the limited consideration model, and the identified set for consideration probabilities is a point only with unbounded support.
papers.q: How do exogenous consideration set models relate to classic discrete choice and extended random utility models?
papers.contribution: Relates the consideration set additive random utility model to classic and extended models and characterizes identification and welfare results.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: identification in consideration set models of discrete choice.

papers.title: Direct and Indirect Effects of Vaccines: Evidence from COVID-19
papers.q: How large are the direct and indirect effects of COVID-19 vaccines, and how far does the externality extend?
papers.summary: Vaccination reduces cases by 80% directly. Protection spills over to close contacts, with a household indirect effect about three-fourths as large as the direct effect, but not to schoolmates.
papers.contribution: Uses near-universal microdata from one state and the six-month delay between vaccine eligibility at ages 11 and 12.
papers.conclusion: Vaccine reach matters when designing infectious disease policy.
papers.ident: Regression discontinuity-style comparison using the six-month delay in vaccine eligibility between ages 11 and 12.
papers.dataDetail: Nearly universal microdata from a single state.

papers.title: Divine Policy: The Impact of Religion in Government
papers.q: Do faith-based government initiatives shape religiosity and social views?
papers.summary: The initiatives strengthened religiosity and conservative-religious views such as attitudes against homosexuals. The results are robust to contiguous county comparisons and triple differences, and the key mechanism is the establishment of faith-based organizations.
papers.ident: Staggered difference-in-differences across US states, with contiguous-county and triple-difference robustness.
papers.contribution: Exploits the staggered introduction of faith-based initiatives across US states in a difference-in-differences design.
papers.dataDetail: Survey data on religiosity and attitudes and data on nonprofit organizations.

papers.title: Highway to Hitler
papers.summary: Autobahn construction boosted support for Hitler, especially where construction coincided with greater radio availability and in politically unstable regions. Direct local economic benefits are unlikely to explain it.
papers.q: Did the building of the Autobahn boost popular support for Hitler?
papers.contribution: Shows that a visible infrastructure project raised support for an autocratic regime through propaganda rather than direct local economic benefits.
papers.conclusion: Visible infrastructure projects can raise support for autocrats when voters associate them with economic progress and an end to political instability.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences exploiting local Autobahn construction in Nazi Germany.

papers.title: The Returns to Physical Capital in Knowledge Production: Evidence from Lab Disasters

authors.inst: Max Planck Institute for Innovation and Competition

papers.q: What are the returns to specialized and generic physical capital in scientific knowledge production?
papers.summary: Scientists who lose specialized equipment and material they created suffer a persistent reduction in research output, whereas losing generic capital leads to recovery. Scientists in older labs are more likely to change research direction and recover.
papers.contribution: Exploits adverse events in research laboratories to compare losses of specialized and generic physical capital.
papers.conclusion: Investments in own physical capital yield lasting returns but also create path dependence.
papers.ident: Event-study exploiting adverse events in research laboratories.

papers.title: Multi-horizon test for market frictions

authors.inst: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.summary: Proposes a multi-horizon test for market frictions.

papers.title: Informal fiscal systems in developing countries

authors.inst: Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab

papers.summary: Studies informal fiscal systems in developing countries.

papers.title: Markups Across Space and Time
papers.q: How do retail markups behave across space and time?
papers.summary: Markups are relatively stable over time and mildly procyclical, with large regional dispersion and a positive correlation with local income. Regional differences come from the assortment of goods sold, not from deviations from uniform pricing. A simple model is consistent with these facts.
papers.ident: Descriptive: retail markups from gross margins across sector, firm and product levels.
papers.contribution: Provides direct evidence on retail markups measured by gross margins at the sector, firm and product levels.
papers.dataDetail: Retail gross margin data.

papers.title: Culture and Gender Differences in Honesty
papers.q: Do gender differences in honesty reflect innate traits or social norms across societies?
papers.summary: Gender differences in honesty emerge mainly in Western societies, where women report stronger honesty norms, and are absent in non-Western societies. They are transmitted across generations and narrow as countries become wealthier.
papers.contribution: Uses global experimental and survey data to compare gender differences in honesty across Western and non-Western societies.
papers.conclusion: Gender differences in honesty are better explained by socialisation than innate traits.
papers.ident: Cross-societal comparison of experimental honesty behavior and survey honesty norms by gender.
papers.dataDetail: Global experimental and survey data.

papers.title: Resisting social conformity pressure: Impact of a gender norms intervention for adolescents in Somalia
papers.q: Does a gender norms intervention for adolescents in Somalia help them resist social conformity pressure?
papers.summary: Evaluates the impact of a gender norms intervention for adolescents in Somalia on resisting social conformity pressure.

papers.title: Seizing central bank assets?
papers.q: What are the global macroeconomic effects of freezing or seizing central bank assets?
papers.summary: The freeze on Russia's central bank assets is of rarely seen scale, and non-belligerent countries have never seized such assets to finance reconstruction in a third country during a war. Seizure can harm the sanctioning country, raising its government bond interest rates, and extra interest payments could exceed the seized amount after about three years.
papers.ident: Quantitative: three-country DSGE model of sanctions on central bank assets, with a historical database.
papers.contribution: Builds a database of freezes and seizures of central bank assets from 1914 to 2024 and a three-country DSGE model of sanctions.
papers.dataDetail: Database of central bank asset freezes and seizures, 1914-2024.

papers.title: Robustness to missing data: breakdown point analysis
papers.q: How much selection from missing data would overturn a given empirical result?
papers.summary: Selection is measured as divergence between the distributions of complete and incomplete observations. Simulations show finite sample performance, and the method is illustrated on randomized controlled trials with attrition.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: breakdown point analysis of robustness to missing data in GMM models.
papers.contribution: Proposes the breakdown point, the minimal selection needed to overturn a result, with a root-n consistent and asymptotically normal estimator for any GMM-identified conclusion.
papers.dataDetail: Illustration on several randomized controlled trials with attrition.

papers.title: Data-driven policy learning for continuous treatments

authors.inst: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen
Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.q: How can optimal policies for continuous treatments be learned from observational data?
papers.summary: For known and unknown propensity scores, the learned policy maximizes empirical or modified empirical welfare, and an oracle inequality for the welfare regret is established.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: policy learning for continuous treatments with kernel welfare estimation.
papers.contribution: Approximates the policy space by finite-dimensional spaces, estimates empirical welfare by kernels and allows machine learning of propensity scores with a tuning algorithm.

papers.title: The Causal Effect of Income on Market Social Responsibility
papers.q: Does higher consumer income cause more socially responsible consumption?
papers.summary: Across three experiments, higher income increases the quantity of socially responsible products purchased and at least slightly raises their share of consumption. Higher total consumption from higher income can increase negative externalities.
papers.contribution: Runs laboratory and online market experiments with exogenously varied consumer incomes and products differing in externality reduction.
papers.ident: Laboratory and online market experiments exogenously varying consumers' incomes.
papers.dataDetail: Three laboratory and online market experiments.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and cognitive inequality
papers.summary: Studies artificial intelligence and cognitive inequality.

papers.title: Empirical welfare maximization with constraints

authors.inst: Centro de Estudios Monetarios y Financieros

papers.contribution: Extends empirical welfare maximization to account for uncertainty in estimating the budget needed to implement the policy.
papers.summary: No rule achieves the highest welfare while satisfying a budget constraint uniformly over a wide range of data generating processes, unlike without a budget constraint. An alternative trade-off rule is proposed and illustrated with Medicaid expansion.
papers.q: How can eligibility policies be chosen from data when the budget needed to implement them is uncertain?
papers.ident: Econometric theory: empirical welfare maximization with budget constraints, illustrated with Medicaid expansion.
papers.dataDetail: Application on Medicaid expansion with imperfect take-up.

papers.title: Social influence and carbon dioxide mitigation
papers.q: Can social influence increase people's willingness to mitigate their carbon impact?
papers.summary: Possibility of influence raises wave-1 willingness to mitigate by about 17%, but not when the choice is observed only after wave-2 choices. Increasing the number of observers does not raise willingness, and most participants overestimate their influence.
papers.ident: Large-scale online experiment varying whether a choice can influence later participants.
papers.contribution: Runs a large online experiment in two waves where wave-1 choices may be observed by wave-2 participants before or after they choose.
papers.conclusion: Effects of social influence are difficult to scale up.
papers.dataDetail: Online experiment with two waves of participants choosing how much of a 10 GBP endowment to spend on mitigation.

papers.title: Bank Information Production Over the Business Cycle
papers.q: How does the quality of banks' private information on loans vary over the business cycle?
papers.contribution: Constructs a novel measure of bank information quality from confidential regulatory data on banks' private risk assessments for US corporate loans.
papers.summary: Information quality improves as local economic conditions deteriorate, especially for new loans, large loans and loans with higher expected losses, and declines during rapid local house price appreciation.
papers.conclusion: The results support theories of countercyclical information production in credit markets.
papers.ident: Panel analysis of private bank risk assessments against local economic conditions.
papers.dataDetail: Confidential regulatory data on banks' private risk assessments for US corporate loans.

papers.title: Marriage Search, Gender Norms and Tradeoffs
papers.summary: Studies marriage search, gender norms and tradeoffs.

papers.title: The Value of Health Insurance: A Household Job Search Approach
papers.q: Does access to free health insurance affect household labor supply decisions in Mexico?
papers.summary: Seguro Popular increased informality among less educated families with children by 3.5%. Estimates show households value it by at most 1.33 per unit of net cost.
papers.contribution: Exploits the 2002 introduction of Seguro Popular, which broke the link between health care and job contract, and estimates a household search model.
papers.ident: Reduced-form estimates around the 2002 introduction of Seguro Popular, plus an estimated household job search model.

papers.title: Barriers to Entry: Decomposing the Gender Gap in Job Search in Urban Pakistan
papers.q: Do supply or demand side constraints drive the gender gap in job search in urban Pakistan?
papers.summary: Employers' gender restrictions constrain women's job opportunities more than supply-side decisions. At higher education levels the barriers relax, letting women qualify for more jobs but at lower salaries, and educated women become more selective.
papers.contribution: Matches data on jobseekers and employers, a job matching platform and an incentivized resume rating experiment in Lahore.
papers.ident: Decomposition using matched jobseeker, employer and platform data plus an incentivized resume rating experiment.
papers.dataDetail: Representative samples of jobseekers and employers, job platform data and resume experiment in Lahore.

papers.title: Selection into Entrepreneurship, Income Mobility and Firm Performance
papers.summary: Top personal income individuals are much more likely to start incorporated businesses, with no similar selection by parental income, though over half of new entrepreneurs have entrepreneurial parents. Entrepreneurship brings a similar 20% income gain across the distribution, but firm productivity and job creation rise with personal income.
papers.q: Who selects into entrepreneurship in Finland, and how does it relate to income mobility and firm performance?
papers.contribution: Uses full-population Finnish data to study selection into entrepreneurship by personal and parental income and firm outcomes.
papers.ident: Descriptive: comparison of new entrepreneurs with comparable wage earners by personal and parental income.
papers.dataDetail: Full-population data from Finland.

papers.title: In the Land of AKM: Explaining the Dynamics of Wage Inequality in France

authors.inst: Institut National de la Statistique et des Etudes Economiques
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.contribution: Uses a newly constructed quasi-exhaustive matched employer-employee database and a simple correction for limited mobility bias in AKM estimates.
papers.summary: Between-firm inequality increased over 2002-2019, mainly due to growing clustering of workers with similar market value, associated with increasing occupational specialization within firms.
papers.q: What explains the dynamics of wage inequality in France through firm contributions?
papers.conclusion: Bias-corrected AKM estimates matter for capturing wage inequality dynamics, with both job types and unobserved individual traits contributing.
papers.ident: Bias-corrected AKM two-way fixed effects decomposition of wage inequality.
papers.dataDetail: Quasi-exhaustive French matched employer-employee data, 2002-2019.

papers.title: Patents to Products: Product Innovation and Firm Dynamics
papers.q: How do patents translate into product innovation and firm dynamics in consumer goods?
papers.summary: More than half of product innovations come from non-patenting firms, and patent filings are followed by product introductions, a link that weakens with firm size. Patents of market leaders yield revenue premiums beyond their own product introductions and deter competitors' innovation.
papers.contribution: Matches patents to products using natural language methods on product descriptions and patent texts, and builds a growth model of strategic patenting.
papers.conclusion: Larger firms' strategic patenting dampens innovation and slows creative destruction.
papers.ident: NLP matching of patents to products, with a growth model of strategic patenting.
papers.dataDetail: Patent texts and consumer goods product descriptions.

papers.title: Exporting, Wage Profiles, and Human Capital: Evidence from Brazil
papers.q: How does exporting shape workers' experience-wage profiles and human capital in Brazil?
papers.summary: Experience-wage profiles are steeper at exporters than non-exporters, and steeper at exporters shipping to high-income destinations. Human capital growth explains half of the profile differences and half of real income gains from trade openness.
papers.contribution: Combines employer-employee and customs data with a model of wage bargaining, export entry and human capital accumulation.
papers.ident: Structural: model of worker-firm bargaining, export entry and human capital accumulation, matched to Brazilian data.
papers.dataDetail: Brazilian employer-employee and customs data for manufacturing.

papers.title: The Impact of Dynamic Prices on Electric Vehicle Public Charging Demand: Evidence from a Nationwide Natural Field Experiment
papers.q: How do dynamic prices affect public electric vehicle charging demand?
papers.summary: A 40% reduction in charging costs raised platform-wide charging activity by 117%, and a 15% cut raised it by 30%. About half the increase reflects substitution between charging apps.
papers.ident: Natural field experiment randomizing price reductions across chargers and customers.
papers.contribution: Runs a large natural field experiment in the United Kingdom with about 110,000 customers and 60% of public charging infrastructure.
papers.conclusion: Dynamic pricing for public EV charging generates large consumer welfare gains.
papers.dataDetail: About 110,000 EV customers on a UK public charging network.

papers.title: Learning and the Emergence of Nonlinearity in Financial Markets
papers.summary: Non-normal beliefs make prices generically display left skew, time-varying and skewed volatility, a relation with price levels and long memory. A simple calibration with iid fundamentals shocks fits well, and regression tests support the mechanism.
papers.ident: Theory: filtering model of investor learning with non-normal beliefs, calibrated to stock returns.
papers.q: Why do stock returns display nonlinearities such as crashes and skewed, persistent volatility?
papers.contribution: Shows in a general filtering model that investors learning about latent fundamentals and believing crashes are possible generates these nonlinearities.
papers.dataDetail: Stock returns.

papers.title: The Cost of State-Building: Evidence from Germany
papers.summary: Across a geographical discontinuity and across collection points of the same transport, Prussian municipalities were significantly more efficient at deporting German Jews, and also better at providing public goods and collecting taxes. Just before the Nazis, they were not differentially anti-Semitic.
papers.ident: Geographic discontinuity at the border of formerly Prussian and non-Prussian Germany.
papers.q: Can state capacity built for development be co-opted for repression, as with the deportation of German Jews under the Nazis?
papers.contribution: Uses the differential build-up of state capacity between formerly Prussian and non-Prussian parts of Germany as a natural experiment.
papers.conclusion: Democratic oversight and aspects of bureaucratic culture can mitigate future abuse of state building projects.
papers.dataDetail: Municipality-level data on deportations, public goods and taxes in Germany.

papers.title: From RANK to HANK, without FIRE
papers.q: How can macroeconomic models be augmented with realistic expectations frictions in place of full information rational expectations?
papers.summary: Clarifies partial- and general-equilibrium effects of informational frictions and their interaction with the Intertemporal Keynesian Cross and strategic complementarity, and reviews lessons for business cycles and policy.
papers.ident: Theory: framework for expectations frictions in representative-agent and heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models.
papers.contribution: Distills the common essence of alternatives to FIRE and develops a new tractable specification for RANK and HANK models.

papers.title: How Good is International Risk Sharing? Stepping Outside the Shadow of the Welfare Theorems

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.q: How efficient is international risk sharing when the real exchange rate does not measure relative consumption costs?
papers.contribution: Develops a methodology measuring relative costs of consumption robust to the disconnect between exchange rates, relative prices and quantities.
papers.summary: Relative consumption growth across regions correlates much more with computed shadow prices than with real exchange rates, suggesting allocation closer to efficient risk sharing. A decentralization with segmented foreign exchange markets and pricing-to-market rationalizes this.
papers.ident: Structural: shadow price measurement and a decentralization with segmented FX markets and pricing-to-market.
papers.dataDetail: Cross-country consumption and prices.

papers.title: Multidimensional Sorting: Comparative Statics
papers.q: How do technological changes affect sorting and earnings in multidimensional assignment models?
papers.contribution: Provides a complete theory of comparative statics showing any technological change decomposes uniquely into a gradient and a divergence-free component.
papers.summary: The gradient component characterizes changes in marginal earnings through a Poisson equation and the divergence-free component characterizes labor reallocation. With US data, equilibrium responses in sorting and earnings to cognitive skill-biased technological change are quantified.
papers.ident: Theory: comparative statics of multidimensional assignment models, quantified on US data.
papers.dataDetail: US data on skills and earnings.

papers.title: Rebuilding Ukraine's Cities: Maximizing Benefits and Minimizing Costs
papers.summary: Ukraine's population is declining, housing demand is shifting from east to west, Kyiv's advantage is growing and its house prices and those of western cities are rising, and cities are slow and congested. Reconstruction costs depend on materials, labor, construction industry organization and procurement and regulation.
papers.q: How can Ukraine's cities be rebuilt to maximize benefits and minimize costs?
papers.contribution: Outlines key facts about Ukrainian cities, a framework for welfare effects of post-war infrastructure allocation, and strategies for shifting the reconstruction cost curve.
papers.conclusion: Three strategies can shift the cost curve: openness, standardization and investing-in-investing.

papers.title: Who Chooses and Who Benefits? The Design of Public School Choice Systems
papers.q: Who chooses and who benefits in public school choice systems, particularly those requiring opt-in participation?
papers.summary: Opt-in systems are the modal design, harder to navigate, and participation is concentrated among more advantaged students. In Los Angeles, lottery estimates show students with the lowest demand for choice schools gain most, so opt-in screens out high-return students and leaves capacity unused.
papers.ident: Admission lotteries and quasi-experimental expansions in access, plus a structural model of system design.
papers.contribution: Uses newly collected national data on choice system design and Los Angeles administrative data, randomized lotteries and quasi-experimental expansions.
papers.dataDetail: Newly collected national data on school choice systems and nearly two decades of Los Angeles Unified School District administrative data.

papers.title: Frosty climate, icy relationships: Cold and intimate partner violence in Peru
papers.q: Does cold weather affect intimate partner violence in Peru?
papers.summary: Studies the relationship between cold temperatures and intimate partner violence in Peru.

papers.title: Understanding the Labor Market Impacts of Place-Based Policies: Evidence from the Opportunity Zone Program
papers.q: What are the labor market effects of the Opportunity Zone place-based program?
papers.summary: OZ designation increases job creation in zones, but much is offset by declines in nearby low-income communities. Longer-run gains in OZ resident employment come from jobs outside zones likely held by new residents, so the benefits to existing residents are limited and reflect spatial reallocation.
papers.contribution: Combines public-use and restricted-access administrative and survey data and a model of firm location, capital-skill complementarity and residential mobility.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences exploiting Opportunity Zone designation across US tracts.
papers.dataDetail: Public-use and restricted-access administrative and survey data for US communities.

papers.title: The Rise of Specialized Financial Products
papers.q: What explains the expansion in the variety of financial products firms use to raise funds?
papers.summary: Differential product adoption across firms explains most variation in funds raised, firms adopting new products raise more funds, and funds from new products are often spread across numerous highly specialized products each used by few firms.
papers.contribution: Combines granular data on security issuance with a parsimonious model of security issuance.
papers.ident: Descriptive facts from granular security issuance data with a model of security issuance.
papers.dataDetail: Granular data on firm security issuance.

papers.title: The global software production network

authors.inst: Centre de Recerca en Economia Internacional

papers.q: Can developing countries benefit from exporting software development services?
papers.summary: Three factors limit exports: large productivity differences within and between countries, a notable decline in trade volumes with distance, and sorting of software developers suggestive of brain drain.
papers.contribution: Analyses data on 2.68 million software projects across 5,200 locations and estimates an economic geography model where locations trade tasks.
papers.ident: Structural: economic geography model of task trade estimated on software project data.
papers.dataDetail: 2.68 million software projects and GitHub users across 5,200 global locations.

papers.title: Multivariate kernel regression in vector and product metric spaces

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.summary: Singularities such as fractal distributions or factor structure give faster convergence, and the results extend to functional regression with multiple functional regressors. Simulations confirm rate improvements and the method is applied to a job training program evaluation.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: nonparametric kernel regression without regressor density.
papers.q: How do kernel regression estimators behave when regressors lack a density, as with mass points or factor structure?
papers.contribution: Derives rates and asymptotic normality of the Nadaraya-Watson estimator for regressors in R^q without density and extends to product metric spaces.
papers.dataDetail: Application re-examines a job training program evaluation.

papers.title: Estimating the welfare cost of labor supply frictions
papers.q: How much would people pay to remove frictions preventing them from working their ideal hours?
papers.summary: Adjustment frictions are costly for any reasonable Hicksian elasticity. Individuals in the US and Germany would pay at least 7% and 4% of income to remove adjustment frictions and tax misperceptions, and adjustment frictions appear more costly than tax misperceptions.
papers.ident: Sufficient statistics: gap between ideal and actual hours and Hicksian elasticity of ideal hours.
papers.contribution: Quantifies willingness to pay using two sufficient statistics: the gap between ideal and actual hours and the Hicksian elasticity of ideal hours.
papers.dataDetail: Data on hours worked in the United States and Germany.

papers.title: CO2 emission regulation and generation allocation with heterogeneous coal-fired generators
papers.q: How does CO2 emission regulation affect generation allocation across heterogeneous coal-fired generators?
papers.summary: Studies CO2 emission regulation and generation allocation among heterogeneous coal-fired generators.

papers.title: Protectionism, evasion and household welfare evidence from Nigeria’s import bans
papers.q: How do Nigeria's import bans affect household welfare given evasion?
papers.summary: Studies protectionism, evasion and household welfare around Nigeria's import bans.

papers.title: Why Is Exclusivity in Broadcasting Rights Prevalent and Why Does Simple Regulation Fail?

authors.inst: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
École Supérieure des Sciences Économiques et Commerciales

papers.q: Why is exclusivity in broadcasting rights prevalent, and do simple regulations improve welfare?
papers.summary: Exclusive allocation is a robust equilibrium outcome but may fail to maximize welfare. Bans on resale and on package bidding do not change the final allocation but redistribute profits along the value chain.
papers.contribution: Shows that convexity of downstream competition profits makes exclusive allocation to the dominant firm the profit-maximizing outcome.
papers.ident: Theory: upstream rights competition among pay-TV firms competing downstream.

papers.title: A Robust Test for Weak Instruments for 2SLS with Multiple Endogenous Regressors
papers.q: How can weak instruments be tested for 2SLS with multiple endogenous regressors under heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation?
papers.summary: The test can use an absolute bias criterion or bias relative to a worst-case benchmark, and extends to individual coefficients. Simulations show it controls size and is powerful, and it is demonstrated on state-dependent fiscal multipliers.
papers.ident: Econometric theory: weak instrument tests for 2SLS with multiple endogenous regressors.
papers.contribution: Develops a robust test for instrument strength based on 2SLS bias that extends Montiel Olea and Pflueger's test to multiple endogenous regressors.
papers.dataDetail: Application to state-dependent fiscal multipliers.

papers.title: Bridges
papers.summary: Local connectivity advantages have negative effects on per capita income, whereas major bridge openings increase per capita economic activity. A narrative reconciles them: infrastructure creates large-scale productivity advantages, but local sorting within early route cities reverses the gradient over small spatial scales.
papers.ident: Quasi-experimental variation from bridges more often built upstream than downstream of tributary confluences.
papers.q: What are the causal effects of land transport infrastructure, using bridges over major rivers in the US?
papers.contribution: Exploits the tendency for bridges to be built upstream rather than downstream of river confluences for quasi-experimental variation in connectivity.
papers.dataDetail: US bridges over major rivers and local economic activity.

papers.title: Consumer durables and monetary policy according to HANK
papers.q: How do consumer durables shape monetary policy transmission in HANK models?
papers.summary: Studies consumer durables and monetary policy in a heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian model.

papers.title: Individualism and the Formation of Human Capital
papers.contribution: Uses international adult skill assessment data and variation between migrants at origin-country, origin-language and person level to identify effects of individualism.
papers.summary: Migrants from more individualistic cultures have higher cognitive skills, larger skill gains, more schooling and more adult education, and earn higher wages with lower unemployment. Individualism explains adult skill formation more than other cultural traits, and results are not explained by selective migration or omitted origin variables.
papers.q: Does individualism shape the formation of human capital?
papers.ident: Epidemiological approach comparing migrants by origin-country, origin-language and person-level individualism.
papers.dataDetail: Largest international adult skill assessment.

papers.title: FBBVA Lecture 2025: Negative Rates and the Effective Lower Bound: Theory and Evidence

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.q: How are negative policy rates transmitted through banks and the open economy, and how does that compare with conventional policy?
papers.contribution: Develops a model with a heterogeneous oligopolistic banking sector using deposit and wholesale funding, embedded in an open-economy macro model, to match evidence on negative rates.
papers.summary: High-deposit banks may see lower margins and profitability and lend less, but low-deposit banks lend more by more than enough to compensate. With the exchange-rate and capital market channels active, transmission of negative rates is only somewhat weaker than conventional policy.
papers.ident: Quantitative: banking model with deposit and wholesale funding embedded in an open-economy macroeconomic model, matched to evidence on negative rates.

papers.title: Foreign and Domestic Firms: Long Run Employment Effects of Export Opportunities
papers.q: What are the long-run employment effects of new export opportunities in a low-income country such as Vietnam?
papers.summary: Employment grew faster in industries most exposed to the US tariff reductions, driven by foreign affiliates of multinationals entering Vietnam, which keep expanding employment even after 16 years. Most foreign entrants are exporters from East Asia, and Vietnam's capacity growth later allows exports to other markets.
papers.contribution: Studies the U.S.-Vietnam Bilateral Trade Agreement's tariff cuts and tracks employment responses over 16 years, highlighting foreign multinational entry.
papers.conclusion: Opportunities created by bilateral agreements are not limited to the signing parties.
papers.ident: Difference-in-differences comparing industries by exposure to US tariff reductions under the US-Vietnam Bilateral Trade Agreement.
papers.dataDetail: Vietnamese industry and firm employment data over 16 years.

papers.title: A choice-based approach to the measurement of inflation expectations

authors.inst: WHU – Otto Beisheim School of Management

papers.q: How can the full distribution of inflation expectations be elicited in a way that is robust across economic conditions?
papers.contribution: Proposes a decision-theory-based choice method to elicit full expectation distributions in standard surveys, as an alternative to density forecasts.
papers.summary: In two large surveys and a lab experiment, the method gives well-defined expectations meeting subjective and objective quality criteria, is not harder or slower to complete and is robust to the state of the economy.
papers.ident: Survey and laboratory experiments testing a new elicitation method for expectations.
papers.conclusion: The method is portable and can elicit other macroeconomic expectations.
papers.dataDetail: Two large surveys and a laboratory experiment.

papers.title: Estimation and inference for CP tensor factor models
papers.summary: Studies estimation and inference for CP tensor factor models.

papers.title: Price Coordination with Asymmetric Information Sharing: Theory and Evidence
papers.q: How can anticompetitive coordination through price-sharing platforms be disrupted when only some firms have access?
papers.summary: Removing only one firm from a platform may be ineffective, but competitive benefits can emerge if at least two firms lack access and the costs of price leadership are high enough. Coordinating price increases is harder when multiple firms cannot quickly observe or respond to rivals' prices.
papers.ident: Theory: model of price coordination with asymmetric platform information sharing.
papers.contribution: Develops a model inspired by the Informed Sources retail gasoline antitrust case to guide remedies for platform-based information sharing.

papers.title: Firm Life-Cycle Learning and Misallocation
papers.contribution: Documents that MRPK dispersion falls with firm age, especially before age five, and builds a model where firms learn their productivity as they age.
papers.summary: Omitting learning can considerably overestimate TFP losses from distortions.
papers.ident: Quantitative: firm dynamics model with learning about productivity and endogenous exit, matched to firm-level panel data.
papers.q: Does firm life-cycle learning explain the dispersion in marginal revenue products of capital and the TFP losses attributed to misallocation?
papers.dataDetail: Firm-level panel data from China.

papers.title: Discretion in Clinical Decision Making: Evidence from Bunching
papers.q: Is discretion in clinical diagnosis of hypertension beneficial?
papers.summary: Bunching appears at 10% of clinics, where 6 to 62% of results expected just above the threshold are recorded just below it. Affected patients have lower cardiovascular risk, suggesting discretion improves classification, partly driven by heuristic thinking.
papers.ident: Bunching estimation at the hypertension diagnostic threshold of 140/90 mmHg, with variation across clinics.
papers.contribution: Uses bunching estimation of blood pressure readings at the hypertension threshold in microdata from 619,907 patients.
papers.dataDetail: Microdata on 619,907 patients in Chile.

papers.title: Income and Child Maltreatment: Evidence from a Discontinuity in Tax Benefits

authors.inst: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.contribution: Exploits a discontinuity in child-related tax benefits with twenty years of linked administrative data from California.
papers.summary: A one-time $1,000 transfer to low-income households reduces child protection referrals by 3% and days in foster care by 7% in the first three years of life, with effects persisting through at least age 8.
papers.q: What is the effect of income on child maltreatment?
papers.ident: Regression discontinuity in child-related tax benefits giving similar families different refunds in the child's first year.
papers.dataDetail: Twenty years of linked administrative data from California on child protection system involvement.

papers.title: Multinational Enterprises and Corporate Labor Share
papers.q: How do multinational enterprises influence the labor share in their home countries?
papers.summary: Flood disruptions to Thai subsidiaries of Japanese multinationals created a negative foreign productivity shock that raised labor share in Japan. The model quantifies the long-run effect of Thai productivity growth on Japan's labor share.
papers.ident: 2011 Thailand floods as a natural experiment, with an IV based on flood exposure.
papers.contribution: Uses the 2011 Thailand floods as a natural experiment and a model with international factor substitution to estimate the elasticity between domestic labor and foreign inputs.
papers.conclusion: Expanding global production networks can shift labor-capital balances.
papers.dataDetail: Japanese multinational firms and their Thai subsidiaries.

papers.title: The Long-Term Impact of High School Financial Education: Evidence from Brazil
papers.summary: Treated students are less likely to borrow from expensive sources or to repay loans late, and shift from formal jobs to microenterprise ownership.
papers.ident: Randomized controlled trial of a financial education program in 892 high schools, with nine years of follow-up.
papers.q: What is the long-term impact of high school financial education in Brazil?
papers.contribution: Follows an RCT across 892 high schools, using administrative data on 16,000 students over nine years.
papers.dataDetail: Administrative data for 16,000 Brazilian students over nine years.

papers.title: Bring a friend: Leveraging financial and peer support to improve women’s reproductive agency in India
papers.q: Do subsidies combined with peer support improve women's reproductive agency in India?
papers.summary: The subsidy increased clinic visits and led women to seek company, but combining it with peer support raised contraceptive use, reduced pregnancy and strengthened reproductive agency and peer engagement. Women facing more intrahousehold opposition benefited more.
papers.contribution: Experimentally evaluates subsidized family planning services with and without the ability to invite and incentivize others to the clinic.
papers.ident: Randomized experiment offering subsidized family planning services with or without peer invitation and incentives.
papers.dataDetail: Women in India offered subsidized services at a local clinic.

papers.title: Expressways, market access, and industrial development in China: Using walled-city panel instrumental variables of minimum spanning tree

authors.inst: Macau University of Science and Technology

papers.q: How do expressways affect market access and industrial development in China?
papers.contribution: Uses walled-city panel instrumental variables based on a minimum spanning tree.
papers.summary: Studies the effect of expressways on market access and industrial development in China using a walled-city panel instrumental variable.

papers.title: Self-Justified Equilibria: Existence and Computation

authors.inst: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.summary: The active subspace approach reduces dimensionality and improves forecasting accuracy, and the method computes equilibria efficiently in high-dimensional overlapping generations models with aggregate shocks.
papers.ident: Theory: temporary equilibria with optimal forecasting functions, with numerical computation in overlapping generations models.
papers.q: Can self-justified equilibria replace rational expectations equilibria in tractable heterogeneous-agent general equilibrium models?
papers.contribution: Introduces self-justified equilibria with mean-squared optimal forecasting functions, gives existence conditions and a simulation-based computational method using active subspaces.

papers.title: The price of intelligence: How should socially-minded firms price and deploy AI?
papers.q: How should socially-minded firms price and deploy AI?
papers.summary: Studies how socially-minded firms should price and deploy artificial intelligence.
